summary.en: Armed clashes and intercommunal violence continue across South Sudan, with attacks by rebel and SPLA-IO forces targeting civilians in Tonj East, Warrap State and Greater Pibor, while worshippers were attacked in Gorom refugee camp and a teen was killed for refusing an arranged marriage. UNMISS is supporting deterrence efforts in Tonj East and calling for stronger civilian protection during a visit to Unity, and the Gender Ministry has raised concerns about violence against women and children ahead of a 16 Days campaign. President Kiir travelled to Ethiopia and held high-level investment talks with Saudi Arabia in Riyadh, while a US senator warned that Uganda is playing a destabilising role in the country. The Crisis Group urged African intervention to resolve the crisis and the UNDP resident representative issued a message of solidarity. There were 2 battle-related deaths in 2024, according to UCDP.
summary.nb: Væpnede sammenstøt og vold mellom folkegrupper fortsetter over hele Sør-Sudan, med angrep fra opprørs- og SPLA-IO-styrker som retter seg mot sivile i Tonj East, Warrap-stat og Greater Pibor, mens tilbedere ble angrepet i Gorom flyktningleir og en tenåring ble drept for å ha nektet et arrangert ekteskap. UNMISS støtter avskrekkingsarbeid i Tonj East og oppfordrer til sterkere sivile beskyttelsestiltak under et besøk i Unity, og Kjønnsdepartementet har uttrykt bekymring for vold mot kvinner og barn i forkant av en 16‑dagers kampanje. President Kiir reiste til Etiopia og holdt høyt nivå investeringssamtaler med Saudi-Arabia i Riyadh, mens en amerikansk senator advarte om at Uganda spiller en destabiliserende rolle i landet. Crisis Group oppfordret til afrikansk intervensjon for å løse krisen og UNDP-representanten i landet sendte en solidaritetsmelding. Det var 2 dødsfall knyttet til kamper i 2024, ifølge UCDP.

background.title: South Sudanese Civil War
background.extract: The South Sudanese Civil War was a multi-sided civil war in South Sudan fought from 2013 to 2018 between government and opposition forces. The civil war caused rampant human rights abuses, including forced displacement, ethnic massacres, and killings of journalists by various parties. Since the war's end, South Sudan has been governed by a coalition formed by leaders of the former warring factions, Salva Kiir and Riek Machar. The country continues to recover from the war while experiencing ongoing and systemic ethnic violence.
